review.notes: Recorded as 'ruling', not 'engine': the difference lives in this card's own effect flags, not in a global rule-profile setting, so a rule-profile flag would not reproduce it and the variant is not redundant. Chronology is unresolved - nothing in the packet or the shared briefs dates when Limiter Removal's Damage Step window changed. Conflicting evidence preserved: the text lineage suggests a behavioural axis that neither implementation distinguishes. The baseline text v2 (DB1-EN179, 2004-10-12) doubles the ATK of Machine monsters 'on your side of the field when you activate this card'; v6 (DL16-EN013, 2013-07-01) and v7 (SDGR-EN022, 2014-10-16) read 'you controlled at both the activation and resolution of this card'; v5/v8/v9 read 'you currently control'. The script diff touches only the Damage Step flag, the condition, and constant spellings, so neither the GOAT nor the modern script implements an activation-time snapshot, and no functional change is claimed on that axis. Constant-only differences confirmed equal: RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END = RESET_EVENT|RESETS_STANDARD|RESET_PHASE|PHASE_END (constant.lua:300), and RESET_PHASE|PHASE_END vs RESET_PHASE+PHASE_END are the same value. Everything from v2 through v9 (LEDD-ENB18, 2017-10-05, the pinned cdb text) is otherwise cosmetic ('Machine-Type' -> 'Machine', 'until the End Phase' <-> 'until the end of this turn').

event.historical_text: Double the ATK of all face-up Machine-Type monsters that are on your side of the field when you activate this card. During the End Phase, destroy all Monster Cards that were affected by this effect.
event.summary: Period Damage Step legality, carried per-card by the effect's own permission flag: the GOAT script swaps EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP (0x4000) for EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_CAL (0x8000) on the activation effect, moving the window inside the Damage Step in which Limiter Removal may be activated - PHASE_DAMAGE (0x20) and PHASE_DAMAGE_CAL (0x40) are distinct phases in ocgcore, so the two flags license different sub-steps. The accompanying condition swap is a no-op: the variant's inline 'Duel.GetCurrentPhase()~=PHASE_DAMAGE or not Duel.IsDamageCalculated()' is logically identical to the modern aux.StatChangeDamageStepCondition ('not (Duel.IsPhase(PHASE_DAMAGE) and Duel.IsDamageCalculated())', CardScripts utility.lua:1412), and the hint timing follows the flag. 25 of upstream's 191 GOAT scripts carry the same substitution, so it is a systematic period-Damage-Step encoding rather than a per-card quirk.
